posts.title: Latest news about Lego animal moulds
posts.text: To be fair, Lion Knight’s Castle only offered us a few animals but it got us so many minifigures. And they brought back horse’s barding piece back. As for Venice Neighbhorhood, I don’t think it’s that unreasonable why the set has so many minfigures. I see that they recolor a few parts from dead themes like Golden Eagle’s beak from Monkie Kid and Nightmare Emperor’s helmet from DreamZzz. They spent budget on printed elements, such as one for clock tower in Venice set. And they did print a game console piece as a mask. I think recoloring python might be little expensive for this set’s budget. Therefore, I am echoing what I j said in my preivous part above - there is a glimpse of hope that we will see new color for pigeon.

posts.text: I was also surprised by the recolors of the Nightmare Emperor's helmet (from Dreamzzz) and the Golden Winged Eagle's beak (from Monkie Kid) for the carnival costumes. I dunno, I feel like there's a certain appropriateness to a hardware store since it's the kind of business that can actually be involved in building/architecture itself. It's easy to think of ways a hardware store can be used in interconnected storytelling with other shops/businesses (as a source for parts used for renovations or repairs).

posts.title: [MOC] Impossible Clock
posts.text: The 1:12 gearing mechanism for minutes to hours is in the "floating" hub supported only by the minute hand, and holds its orientation by gravity. It was an interesting challenge getting this light enough and appropriately balanced. Once again, splat gears were extremely useful. I'm appreciating them more and more. It's also very nice that more gears are readily available in black now (specifically, 16t spur and 12t half bevel).

posts.title: LEGO Star Wars Set Discussion 2026 - READ FIRST POST!!!
posts.text: I too hope we get a Briefcase Clanker minifig. (Watch Inbetweeners!!) But not as much as I hope for a TIE Avenger!!!!!!! Honestly i would accept them being FO Remnant mercenaries. There were dozens of Resurgent class FO Star Destroyers in the galaxy, they can't all have blown up in the span of 10 minutes. Plus we don't know for sure what happened to the Xyston that destroyed Kijimi. And that's not even accounting for all the bases, strongholds and garrisons which would have to exist for them to maintain control. posts.title: A Practical Lego Mechanical Skeleton Clock | Deco Clock II
posts.text: Introducing Deco Clock II, a Lego mechanical skeleton clock that can fit easily into any stand or shelf. Long story short, a previous wall clock I published on YouTube did not perform well in the long term because of inherent flaws in the structure and using parts that were used instead of new. Hanging a clock structure off a wall with a heavy pendulum and weight demands a great amount of structural engineering, and I wanted something that had less uncertainty with how sturdy the structure was. This saga has ostensibly turned into a second version of this clock, one which is designed with long-term performance, practicality, and similar aesthetics in mind. I want people to easily be able to get into the hobby, and this clock is designed with long-term performance and ease-of-set up in mind. In my opinion, most mechanical Lego clocks fail at many of the listed aspects below (aside from some of David’s and KEvron’s pieces, and even those require custom stands or shelves). Yes, this stand is one you need to supply yourself. Although, it can either be easily bought or assembled in whatever kit it comes with online, does not need any modifications to your walls, does not need any custom tools or jobs, can easily be moved around, and can even display other things on the lower shelves within the stand. A clock with that in mind needs the following things, which this one satisfies: Actually tells accurate time. Has instructions Has good, reliable mechanisms (The class-leading David Ziemkiewicz’s 64t grasshopper escapement). Easily modifiable Runs for a full day 100% original Lego Looks like it can be a real decoration. No electronics The structure it sits on does not require any tools or custom jobs. The entire thing can easily be moved to different areas. The structure is sound and made with sturdy Technic bricks rather than feeble Technic lift arms. The large PDF guide will be on Rebrickable soon and has everything you need to know to set it up. Guide for now here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/19oCEW1kYmrOvCebuSBKqhcnur89A68zu/view?usp=drive_link I’m happy to answer any questions at: therealfabulousfox@gmail.com. See the full, detailed video on my YouTube channel.

posts.title: [MOC / Ideas] "Just a Toy?" – Engineering a Working Analog Clock with Concentric Rings
posts.text: @Davidz90 Thanks a lot for sharing all these construction details and photos with me! It’s really interesting to see that, even though we took different paths, many of the solutions you explored are identical to the ones I tested and, in some cases, adopted myself (such as offsetting the two rings by 45° and using rollers at the base). I also tried using the outer grooves to constrain and guide the rings, supporting their weight with bearings made from rubberized wheels. For the groove guides, I used the **1x1 Round Tiles with Bar / Pin (Part #20482)**. In the end, I moved away from that approach and allowed the rings to rest naturally by gravity on the support wheels, held in place by the drive pinion. In early versions, I used two 8t pinions (for a higher reduction ratio and less required torque), but after encountering a few issues with mesh and stability, I switched to a single 12t drive pinion. I'll definitely experiment with the magnetic hand concept for fun, though as you noted, it won't be something I can submit on the LEGO Ideas portal. Thanks again for sharing your work!
